t: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Thermal Occupancy Desk — Simple
name: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Thermal Occupancy Desk — Simple
title: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Thermal Occupancy Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Room temperature glows: the desk computes the thermal photon occupancy n̄ = 1/(e^{hc/λkT}−1) per mode. At 1550 nm and 300 K it's ~10⁻¹³ — negligible; at 10 µm it's 2.7 — the wavelength decides whether room-temp quantum optics is easy or hard.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Thermal occupancy at 1550 nm, 300 K = 3.65e-14 photons. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Photonic Quantum Computer (Room-Temp): Thermal Photon Noise vs. Fixed Filtering Mode
real_world_basis: Thermal occupancy math is the real physics of room-temperature quantum optics.
signature_version: Signature version: the fixed-filtering thermal desk — the chapter's Fixed Filtering Mode as the rejection target, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the wavelength is the design variable — pick where thermal is negligible.
math_note: Thermal occupancy at 1550 nm, 300 K: 3.65e-14 photons [verified]; Thermal occupancy at 10 µm, 300 K: 0.0083 photons [verified]
safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a mid-IR design that ignores the glow.
how_it_works: Plug the wavelength and temperature into the Bose-Einstein occupancy. The demo tables the telecom to mid-IR bands.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time

t: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Filter Extinction Budget — Simple
name: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Filter Extinction Budget — Simple
title: Room-Temp Photonic Quantum Computer: Filter Extinction Budget — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Filters reject the noise: the desk budgets the extinction ratio needed to suppress thermal and pump photons below the signal. The extinction is priced in dB per stage — rejection is engineered, not hoped.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Stages for 100 dB at 25 dB each = 4 stages. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Photonic Quantum Computer (Room-Temp): Thermal Photon Noise vs. Fixed Filtering Mode
real_world_basis: Extinction budgeting is the real basis of quantum photonic filtering.
signature_version: Signature version: the fixed-filtering extinction desk — the chapter's mode as the extinction target, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: measure the real filter curve — catalog extinction is at the center wavelength only.
math_note: Stages for 100 dB at 25 dB each: 4 stages [verified]; Surviving noise after 100 dB: 1.0e-10 fraction [verified]

math_check.label: Stages for 100 dB at 25 dB each

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a filter specified at one wavelength for a broadband job.
how_it_works: Compute the required suppression from the noise-to-signal ratio, divide by per-stage extinction for the stage count. The demo filters a heralded source.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
